steps.note: Use an RFQ stage rather than the default Auction stage.
Apply the first available RFQ pricing template before adding line items.
Create multiple line items so per-line lowest-price comparison can be exercised.
Commit a valid bidding schedule before publishing.
Invite the two vendors required for competing quotes.
Publish the RFQ so vendors can submit bids.
Confirm the RFQ reached a published project page.
Submit the first vendor's initial quote.
Confirm the first vendor's quote was accepted.
Submit a competing quote from the second vendor.
Confirm the second vendor's quote was accepted.
Submit a revised quote from the first vendor, establishing a previous bid for comparison.
Confirm the revised quote was accepted.
Open the RFQ Responses view and confirm both vendor response columns are present.
Check for the response view's L1 labeling, while the catalog cannot assert its per-line green styling.
Ensure the comparison screen has no rendering errors or broken values.
